title: Structure, Evolution, and Mitochondrial Genome Analysis of Representatives of the Families  Mactridae and Veneridae (Mollusca: Bivalvia)
content: Based on the nucleotide sequences of the mitochondrial genome (mitogenome) of specimens tak-en from three specimens of Chinese surf clam, Mactra chinensis, the investigation was performed using approaches from genomics, molecular phylogenetics, and evolutionary genetics. The mito-genome structure of studied mollusks, as in many other invertebrates, appears to be much more variable than in vertebrates and includes variation in gene order, duplications, and deletions, par-ticularly among tRNA genes. The investigated mitogenomes of 30 representatives of the order Venerida have variable sizes and provided useful information for species identification and mo-lecular phylogenetic reconstruction with distinct resolution for families Mactridae and Veneridae as well as for genera and species level taxa. Mitogenome sequences obtained from GenBank and generated in this study were examined to determine whether they originated from females (F) or males (M). Analysis of the new data did not confirm the known drastic differences between the F/M mitogenome lines reported in some other bivalve mollusks. For the 13 protein-coding genes (PCGs) analyzed in 30 mitogenomes from Mactridae and Veneridae, the mean genetic distances (p-distances ± standard error) were (1) 3.61 ± 0.99%, (2) 22.09 ± 0.68%, (3) 23.56 ± 0.54%, and (4) 40.60 ± 0.32% for four comparison groups: (1) individuals of the same species; (2) species within the same genus; (3) species from different genera within the same family; and (4) species from different families within the order, respectively. Phylogenetic reconstructions of the mitogenomes were performed using the combined set of genetic markers, reconstructing datasets based on all genes, only protein-coding genes (PCGs), and only rRNA + tRNA genes. Obtained data on positive pro-portional relationships of genetic distances and taxa ranks in wide variety animal taxa are discussed and supported earlier published generalizations on prevailing geographic mode of speciation in Nature as well as phyletic evolution at molecular marker’s level. The divergence time from the most recent common ancestor (MRCA), estimated using BEAST2 based on the 30 PCGs of mitoge-nomes is close to 339 Mya, placing the estimated divergence in the Carboniferous and potentially earlier. The results also address an important property of protein polypeptides, such as hydropho-bicity and its determination by the purine and pyrimidine nucleotide ratio.
